hens_rule_text: Up to about 4 hens allowed on a typical residential lot (limit rises with lot size) with a Columbus Public Health permit; a poultry education course is reported as a permit condition.
permit_notes: A permit from Columbus Public Health is required, reported at a $100 fee valid for 4 years (an older $50 fee is also cited by some sources); completion of a certified poultry education course is reported as a requirement.
setback_notes: Coop must be at least 20 ft from any neighboring residence and 5 ft from property lines.
coop_rules: Coop must be kept clean and in good repair; as of 2026, rodent-proofing with half-inch hardware cloth and an impervious floor (concrete or treated wood) is reported as a new requirement.
zoning_notes: Rules apply to residential lots citywide, with the hen cap scaling with lot size; slaughter on the property is reported as not permitted.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: BackYard Chickens forum, Columbus Ohio Chicken Ordinance
CoopCraft Guide, Ohio Backyard Chicken Laws by City

research_notes: No Columbus Public Health page or municipal code section was directly opened; all figures come from secondary sites summarizing the permit program, and they disagree on the fee amount ($50 vs $100), so the permit cost, exact code section and the 2026 rodent-proofing rule are unverified against a primary source.
